o.text: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish طیاره (tayyare), itself derived from the Arabic ط ي ر (ṭ y r, “related to flying”). Attested no earlier than 1910s.
From Proto-Common Turkic *ēder. Cognate with Bashkir эйәр (iyär), see there for more cognates.

to pass, to go by, to elapse, to slip by (of time)

o.text: From Proto-Turkic *öt- (“to pass by, pass through”). Cognate with Chuvash вит (vit).
From Proto-Turkic *öt- (“to sing (of birds); to say; to ask, request”). Cognate with Turkish ötmek, Chuvash авӑт (avăt, “to sing (of birds)”).

Likely a calque of Russian словообразова́тельный (slovoobrazovátelʹnyj).
By surface analysis, söz (“word”) + düzəlt- (“to form”) + -ici.
From Arabic بَشَرِيَّة (bašariyya). By surface analysis, bəşər + -iyyət.
From Arabic فَوْق + الطَّبِيعِيّ (fawq + aṭ-ṭabīʕiyy, literally “above the natural”). By surface analysis, fövqəl- + təbii.
